The story relies heavily on summary and exposition rather than dramatized scenes. Nearly the entire narrative—covering a span of three years—is told by compressing time, recounting events from a distance, and providing background information about the building, the faculty, and the ongoing construction phases. While there are brief flashes of specific moments (such as Dr. Amsel discovering the water or Tomás catching rain in a trash can), they are integrated into the overarching summary rather than played out in real-time. There is only one very brief exchange of direct dialogue at the very end of the story.
